newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas sees four deals done in thin session.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas sees four deals done in thin session.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract saw a disappointing afternoon session on Tuesday, with only 35 lots traded in just four separate transactions.

All were done late, with 10 lots each in July and August trading at 1548 GMT, followed by a further 10 lots in August at 1557 GMT, and a final trade of five lots in March done just seconds before the contract closed. The contract is open in the afternoon from 1400 GMT to 1600 GMT.

"It's been a bit disappointing," said a broker. "But there's quite a lot of buying interest there." He added that there were both bids and offers seen across the board, but "they didn't come together this afternoon."

The buying interest for March was down to 9.00 pence a therm by the close. A trade done there at the end of the day brought the price back down to Monday's settlement level after earlier March trade had been done as high as 9.70 pence a therm.
Price movements in other contracts were seen as unrepresentative as they reflected such a small volume of trade.

Although there was a spate of bids and offers posted on the screen in the dying seconds of the contract, especially in the outer months, they remained too far apart to make trade a serious possibility and in the end four separate trades in the afternoon could not be improved upon.
